children.translated_text: She who is most capable of removing the irresistible torment of the mind,
the source of the entire mass of bliss in the world—I take refuge in her. // 1 //
The wise <s>Keśava</s>, son of <s>Sadānanda</s>, born of <s>Bhaṭṭa Keśava</s>,

children.text: yajurvit keśavaḥ prāha kiñcit sāṃkhye yathāmati // 2 //
children.translated_text: a knower of the <s>Yajurveda</s>, expounds something of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> according to his understanding. // 2 //

body.text:
iha dvividhaṃ tattvaṃ prakṛtiḥ puruṣaśceti |
prakṛtireva pradhānamityabhidhīyate sattvāditriguṇā nityeti prakṛtisvarūpalakṣaṇam |
vikārarahitattvācca nityaiveyam |
puruṣe ativyāptivāraṇāya sattvāditriguṇetyuktam |
sattvādayastrayo guṇā yasyā iti vigrahaḥ |
mahadāditattvānāmapi triguṇātmakatvāt tatrātiprasaṅgavāraṇāya nityeti |
taṭasthalakṣaṇaṃ tu jagadupādānakāraṇaṃ prakṛtiriti |
tathāhi vimataṃ sukhaduḥkhamohasāmānyopādānakaṃ niyamena tadanvitasvabhāvatvāt yanniyamena yadanvitasvabhāvaṃ tat tatsāmānyopādānakaṃ yathā mṛtsāmānyānvitasvabhāvaṃ ghaṭaśarāvādi tathāhi kācana taruṇī kasyacit kāntasya sukhamutpādayati kasyacinmohaṃ kasyaciddveṣamiti tatkasya hetostaṃ taṃ prati sukhaduḥkamohātmakasattvarajastamasāmāvirbhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Here there are two kinds of <s>tattva</s> (reality): <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness). <s>Prakṛti</s> itself is called <s>Pradhāna</s> (the chief principle). The essential definition of <s>Prakṛti</s> is that she possesses the three <s>guṇas</s>—<s>sattva</s> (goodness), <s>rajas</s> (passion), and <s>tamas</s> (darkness)—and is eternal. She is eternal because she is devoid of modification. The qualifier 'possessing the three <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the rest' is stated to prevent over-extension to <s>Puruṣa</s>. The analysis is: 'that which has the three <s>guṇas</s>, namely <s>sattva</s> and the rest.' Since the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Mahat</s> are also constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, the word 'eternal' is added to prevent over-extension to them. The extrinsic definition (<s>taṭasthalakṣaṇa</s>) is: <s>Prakṛti</s> is the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>) of the world. For the disputed entity [the world] has pleasure, pain, and delusion as its common material cause, because it invariably has a nature pervaded by those [qualities]. Whatever invariably has a nature pervaded by something, that has that thing as its common material cause—just as a pot, a saucer, and the like have a nature invariably pervaded by clay. For example, a certain young woman produces pleasure in a certain lover, delusion in another, and aversion in yet another. Why is this? Because the <s>guṇas</s>—<s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>—whose natures are pleasure, pain, and delusion respectively, manifest differently toward each person.

body.text:
sā ca caturviṃśatidhā prakṛteḥ prathamo mahāniti vikāraḥ pariṇāma iti yāvat mahattattvameva buddhitattvamityabhidhīyate ahamityahaṃkārākhyo mahattattvasya prathamo vikāraḥ tadanantaraṃ pañcatanmātrāḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhākhyā bhavati athākāśādibhūtapañcakaṃ athaikādaśākṣāṇi śrotrasparśanacakṣūrasanaghrāṇavāggudaliṅgakaracaraṇāntaḥkaraṇānyekādaśendriyāṇi bhavanti |
tatra mahattattvamahaṃkāratattvaṃ śabdādyāḥ pañcatanmātrā ityetat tattvasaptakaṃ prakṛtivikṛtibhāvāpannaṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ prati kāryatvamuttarottaraṃ prati kāraṇatvamityarthaḥ |
tathāhi mahattattvaṃ mūlaprakṛteḥ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ cāhaṃkāratattvasya ahaṃkāratattvaṃ tathā mahattattvasya kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca śabdatattvākhyāditanmātraṃ prati tathāhi tadapi pūrvaṃ prati kāryamuttaraṃ prati kāraṇaṃ ceti bodhyam |
ākāśādibhūtapañcakamekādaśendriyāṇītyete punaḥ ṣoḍaśabhāvāśca prakṛtijanyā eva na tu kasyacit prakṛtiḥ tattvāntaropādānarūpatvābhāvāt |
seyaṃ prakṛtiracetanā pariṇāmitvāt |
body.translated_text:
And she [<s>Prakṛti</s>] evolves in twenty-four forms. The first modification from <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One)—'modification' meaning transformation—and <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is also called <s>Buddhi-tattva</s> (the principle of intellect). The first modification of <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is called <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), characterized by the cognition 'I.' Next arise the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), designated as sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. Then the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> (space). Then the eleven sense organs (<s>indriyas</s>): the organs of hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell; the organs of speech, excretion, generation, hands, and feet; and the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>)—these are the eleven <s>indriyas</s>.
Among these, the group of seven <s>tattvas</s>—<s>Mahat-tattva</s>, <s>Ahaṃkāra-tattva</s>, and the five <s>tanmātras</s> beginning with sound—have the status of being both <s>prakṛti</s> (cause) and <s>vikṛti</s> (effect): each preceding one is an effect relative to its prior, and a cause relative to its subsequent. That is: <s>Mahat-tattva</s> is the effect of the root <s>Prakṛti</s> and the cause of <s>Ahaṃkāra-tattva</s>; <s>Ahaṃkāra-tattva</s> is likewise the effect of <s>Mahat-tattva</s> and the cause of the <s>tanmātra</s> beginning with the sound principle—for it too is an effect relative to what precedes and a cause relative to what follows; this should be understood.
The sixteen entities—the five gross elements beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> and the eleven <s>indriyas</s>—are produced by <s>Prakṛti</s> alone and are not the <s>prakṛti</s> (material cause) of anything, because they do not serve as the material cause of any other <s>tattva</s>.
This <s>Prakṛti</s> is unconscious (<s>acetanā</s>), because she is subject to transformation.

body.text:
nanu viṣayāṇāṃ ghaṭādīnāṃ cetanasambandhaḥ sākṣādevāstu kiṃ mahadādipraṇālikayeti cet |
tat kiṃ citireva viṣayabandhanasvabhāvā tathā sati caityanyanityatayā mokṣaḥ kadāpi na syāt |
atha caitanyaṃ prakṛtau pratibimbitaṃ prakṛtiviṣayayostu sākṣāt sambandhaḥ syāt kiṃ mahadādineti cet tathāhi puruṣavannityatayā punaranirmokṣāpattireva |
atha citirviṣayasambaddhasvabhāvā māstu viṣayā eva citisambaddhasvabhāvāḥ santu tathā ca viṣayatirobhāve mokṣaḥ syāditi cet tarhīdaṃ dṛṣṭamiti na syāt sarvathā citisambandhasvābhāvyenāvyavadhānāt |
atha viṣayā indriyadvārā citisambaddhātmānaḥ santu dṛṣṭādṛṣṭavyavahārādi sannikarṣaviprakarṣābhyāmupapatsyata iti cenna vyāsaṅgānupapatteḥ indriyasambaddhe viṣaye jñānotpatterāvaśyakatvāt |
atha vyāsaṅgānupapattyā manaḥ kalpyatāṃ kimahaṃkāreṇa maivaṃ evaṃ ca sati svasmin vyāghrohaṃ varāhohamiti nāropayet kiṃtvindriyaṃ manodvārā citisambaddhaṃ svakīyaṃ naratvameva gṛhṇīyāt |
athaivamahaṃkārostu svapnadaśāyāmāropārthaṃ buddhitattve na mānamasti maivaṃ suṣuptyavasthāyāṃ manovadahaṃkāropi nivṛttavyāpāra eva tathā ca śvāsaprayojakajīvanayoniyatnasya vyāpāraḥ syāditi tadanurodhena buddhitattvasyāpyāvaśyakatvāt tasmādbuddhitattvaṃ parigamena(?) sambaddho viṣayo gajaturagamahiṣādiḥ puruṣeṇa caitanyena sambadhyate tata āsaṃsārabuddhitattvanāśādeva ca mokṣa iti nānirmokṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Let the connection of objects such as pots with consciousness (<s>cetana</s>) be direct — what need is there for the channel of <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) and the rest? [Reply:] Then is consciousness (<s>citi</s>) itself of the nature of being bound to objects? In that case, since consciousness would be non-eternal like its objects, <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) would never be possible. [Objection:] Suppose consciousness is reflected in <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial matter), and there is a direct connection between <s>Prakṛti</s> and objects — what need then for <s>Mahat</s> and the rest? [Reply:] In that case, since [<s>Prakṛti</s>] is eternal like <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious Self), there would again be the fault of non-liberation. [Objection:] Let consciousness not be of the nature of being connected to objects; rather, let the objects themselves be of the nature of being connected to consciousness. And thus, upon the disappearance of objects, <s>mokṣa</s> would occur. [Reply:] In that case, the cognition 'this is seen' would not occur, since, by the objects being invariably of the nature of being connected to consciousness, there would be no interruption [of cognition]. [Objection:] Let the objects be connected to consciousness through the door of the sense organs (<s>indriya</s>); then the distinction between 'seen' and 'unseen' would be accounted for by proximity and distance. [Reply:] No, because the difficulty of attachment (<s>vyāsaṅga</s>) would not be explained, since the arising of knowledge is necessarily [tied to] an object connected to a sense organ. [Objection:] Let <s>manas</s> (mind) be posited to resolve the difficulty of attachment — what need is there for <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego)? [Reply:] Not so; for in that case, one would not superimpose upon oneself [the notion] 'I am a tiger' or 'I am a boar'; rather, the sense organ, connected to consciousness through the door of <s>manas</s>, would apprehend only its own human nature. [Objection:] Let <s>ahaṃkāra</s> then exist for the purpose of superimposition in the dream state; there is no need for the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> (intellect-principle). [Reply:] Not so; for in the state of deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> too, like <s>manas</s>, has ceased its activity; and therefore the activity of the effort-of-life (<s>jīvanayoniyatna</s>) that impels breathing would [need to be accounted for], and in accordance with that, the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> is also necessarily required. Therefore, objects such as elephants, horses, and buffaloes, connected through the channel of <s>buddhi-tattva</s>, are connected with <s>Puruṣa</s>, i.e. consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>); and liberation consists precisely in the destruction of <s>buddhi-tattva</s> for the duration of <s>saṃsāra</s> — hence there is no non-liberation.

body.text:
akāraṇamakāryaṃ ca kūṭasthacaitanyarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ atrāyaṃ puruṣaḥ svayaṃ jyotiriti śrutyā tāvat svaprakāśamātmano 'bhidhīyate svaprakāśaṃ ca vijñānameva tenātmanaḥ svaprakāśatvamabhidadhatīyaṃ śrutirvijñānātmakatāṃ puruṣasyāvedayati |
na ca kṣaṇikasya jñānasya nityapuruṣātmakatvaṃ sambhavatīti jñānasya kṣaṇabhaṅguratvāsiddheḥ vināśavyavahārasya tava ghaṭākāśadivināśavyavahāravadaupādhikatvenāpyupapatteḥ puruṣātiriktacaitanyasvīkartustavāpi mate jñānasya kṣaṇikatve mānābhāvaḥ anyathā kālāntare 'nubhūtasmaraṇānupapattiḥ |
na ca saṃskāro dvāraṃ tatkalpanāpekṣayā jñānasya sthairyakalpanāyāṃ lāghavāt nityatvāccāsau na kasyacidvikāraḥ na vā kāraṇaṃ svaprakāśatvāt yadi hi svaprakāśasyāpyasya prakṛtitvamāśrīyate tarhyetadvikṛtitvenābhimatasyāpi svaprakāśatvamasya vā jaḍatvamāpadyeta samānayoreva prakṛtivikṛtibhāvopalambhāt bhedāgrahācca niṣkriyepi puruṣe kartṛtvābhimānaḥ evaṃ sukhaduḥkhādivyavahāropi tathāhi pariśuddhacaitanyavigrahaḥ prakṛtivikṛtibhāvānapetataṭasthaḥ puṣkarapalāśavannirlepo 'pyantaḥkaraṇākārapariṇataprakṛtitādātmyamavivekalakṣaṇamavidyayā pratipadyate tataścetaretarādhyāsādantaḥkaraṇāvṛttīnāṃ duḥkhādīnāṃ puruṣe puruṣadharmāṇāṃ ciccaitanyādīnāmantaḥkaraṇe 'dhyāsādahaṃ duḥkhītyādivyavahāro bhavatīti |
avidyānāmātāttvikī khyātiḥ sā ca tamoguṇodrekādāvirbhavantī viviktayostādātmyamavabhāsayati |
tataścottareṣāmasmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśānāṃ kleśaśabdābhidheyānāṃ heturavidyeti gīyate |
tatsiddhaṃ nirlepa evāyamiti |
asaṅgo hyayamiti śruterupapadyate ca |
na ca kopyasya vyāpāra iti ālocanaṃ tāvadindriyavyāpāraḥ vikalpastu manasaḥ abhimānohaṃkārasya kṛtyadhyavasāyo buddheḥ |
atha kṛtyadhyavasāyaḥ kṛtimattayā jñānaṃ tatkathamacetanāyā buddheriti buddhiraṃśatrayavatī puruṣoparāgo viṣayoparāgo vyāpārāveśaśceti |
bhavati hi mamedaṃ kartavyamiti tatra mametyaṃśaścetanasya darpaṇanirmalāyā buddheḥ pratibimba upadhānaṃ taccātāttvikameva caitanyena buddhervāstavasambandhābhāvāt yathā darpaṇaṃ mukhasambandhamantareṇāpi puruṣabhramastadvadihāpi |
idamiti viṣayopadhānaṃ tacca vāstavameka indriyapraṇālikayā buddhau jñānarūpaviṣayasambandhāt darpaṇasyeva niḥśvāsābhihatasya malinimā pāramārthikaḥ puruṣoparāgaḥ viṣayoparāgamāhimnā ca kṛtimattayādhyavasāyaḥ ayameva vyāpārāveśaḥ |
atha jñānameva caitanyaṃ kathamanayorbheda iti ucyate kṛtyadhyavasāyalakṣaṇavyāpāraviśiṣṭā buddhirindriyapraṇālikayā buddherviṣayasya ghaṭādeḥ sambandho vṛttiviśeṣastadeva jñānaṃ viṣayoparāgeṇa saha yaḥ puruṣoparāgasyātāttvikaḥ sambandhaḥ sa upalabdhiḥ yathā darpaṇaniṣṭhā malinimā darpaṇapratibimbitamukhe dṛśyate tatheti yāvat |
tathā ghaṭamahaṃ jānāmītyanuvyavasāyākhyopalabdhiriti vibhāvanīyam |
body.translated_text:
<s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self) is of the nature of immutable consciousness (<s>kūṭasthacaitanya</s>), being neither a cause nor an effect. Here, by the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) 'This <s>puruṣa</s> is self-luminous,' the self-luminous nature of the self is declared. And self-luminous means nothing other than consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Therefore, this <s>śruti</s>, in declaring the self-luminous nature of the self, reveals that <s>puruṣa</s> is of the nature of consciousness.
Nor is it possible that momentary knowledge should be the nature of the eternal <s>puruṣa</s> — because the momentariness of knowledge is itself unproven, since the usage of 'destruction' in your view can be explained as merely adventitious, just as the usage of 'destruction' with regard to pot-space (<s>ghaṭākāśa</s>). Even for you who accept consciousness separate from <s>puruṣa</s>, there is no evidence for the momentariness of knowledge in your own system; otherwise, the recollection of what was experienced at another time would be inexplicable.
Nor is <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) the means [of recollection], since the postulation of <s>saṃskāra</s> is less parsimonious than the postulation of the stability of knowledge. And being eternal, it (<s>puruṣa</s>) is not the modification of anything, nor a cause, because it is self-luminous. For if even this self-luminous entity were regarded as <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial matter), then either what is considered its modification would also be self-luminous, or it itself would become insentient — since the relation of <s>prakṛti</s> and modification is observed only between things of the same nature, and because the difference [between them] is not grasped. Even though <s>puruṣa</s> is devoid of action, the notion of agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) [arises in it]. Similarly, there is also the usage of pleasure, pain, and so forth. For thus: <s>puruṣa</s>, whose form is pure consciousness, who stands apart untouched by the relation of <s>prakṛti</s> and its modifications — like a lotus leaf [untouched by water] — though unattached, through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), characterized by non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>), apprehends an identity with <s>prakṛti</s> as it transforms into the form of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ). From that, through the mutual superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) of the modifications of the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> — suffering and so forth — upon <s>puruṣa</s>, and of the properties of <s>puruṣa</s> — consciousness (<s>cit</s>), <s>caitanya</s>, and so forth — upon the <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>, there arises the usage 'I am suffering' and so forth.
<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is a non-real apprehension (<s>atāttvikī khyāti</s>). And it, becoming manifest from the predominance of the <s>tamas</s> quality (<s>tamoguṇa</s>), causes the identity of two distinct things to appear.
From that, <s>avidyā</s> is declared to be the cause of the subsequent afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) designated by the term <s>kleśa</s>: <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life).
Thus it is established that this [<s>puruṣa</s>] is indeed unattached.
As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'This one is unattached' — and this is coherent.
Nor does it have any activity: perception (<s>ālocana</s>) is the activity of the senses; conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) belongs to the mind (<s>manas</s>); the sense of 'I' belongs to <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego); and the determination of action (<s>kṛtyadhyavasāya</s>) belongs to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect).
Now, if the determination of action is knowledge possessing the character of agency — then how can this belong to the insentient <s>buddhi</s>? <s>Buddhi</s> has three aspects: the coloring by <s>puruṣa</s> (<s>puruṣoparāga</s>), the coloring by the object (<s>viṣayoparāga</s>), and the engagement in activity (<s>vyāpārāveśa</s>).
For there arises: 'This is to be done by me.' In that, the 'by me' aspect is the reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>) of the conscious self in the <s>buddhi</s>, which is clear like a mirror — and that superimposition (<s>upadhāna</s>) is non-real, because there is no actual connection of <s>buddhi</s> with consciousness, just as the [apparent] connection of a person with a mirror even without actual contact with the face — so too here.
The 'this' refers to the superimposition of the object, and that is real in one sense — through the channel of the senses, there is a connection of <s>buddhi</s> with the object in the form of knowledge, just as the tarnishing of a mirror breathed upon is real. The coloring by <s>puruṣa</s>, and by the power of the coloring by the object, the determination possessing the character of agency — this itself is the engagement in activity.
Now, if knowledge itself is consciousness, how is there a difference between the two? It is answered: <s>buddhi</s>, qualified by the activity characterized as the determination of action — the connection of <s>buddhi</s> with the object (such as a pot) through the channel of the senses — this particular modification is knowledge. Together with the coloring by the object, the non-real connection with the coloring by <s>puruṣa</s> is apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>). Just as the tarnish residing in the mirror is seen in the face reflected in the mirror — so it is.
Thus, the apprehension called reflexive awareness (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) — 'I know the pot' — should be understood in this manner.

body.text:
tadeva jñānaṃ sukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmarūpā aṣṭau bhāvā buddhereva ahaṃ jāne sukhītyādisāmānādhikaraṇyapratīteḥ |
nanu yatraite dharmāḥ sa eva cetanaḥ kiṃ na syāditi cenna anityadharmarūpatayā pariṇāmitvāt dharmadharmiṇorabhedāt |
ye punastayorbhedaṃ pratipannāstārkikaprabhṛtayaste tāvannīlo ghaṭā ityādyabhedāvagāhipratyayamapaśyanta upekṣaṇīyāḥ |
nanu pradhānasyācaitanyasya kathaṃ jagatkartṛtvaṃ yat khalu nāmnā rūpeṇa ca vyākriyate taccetanakartṛkaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yathā ghaṭādi |
vivādādhyāsitaṃ ca jagannāmarūpeṇa vyākṛtaṃ tasmāccetanakartṛkamiti sambhāvyate cetano hi buddhāvālikhya nāmarūpe ghaṭā iti nāmnā rūpeṇa ca kambugrīvādinā bāhyaṃ ghaṭaṃ niṣpādayati |
ata eva ghaṭasya nivartyasyāpyantaḥsaṃkalpātmanā siddhasya karmakārakabhāvo ghaṭaṃ karotīti |
body.translated_text:
That very knowledge — the eight states (<s>bhāvas</s>) in the form of pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, merit, demerit — belong to <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) alone, as established by the co-referential cognition 'I know,' 'I am happy,' and so forth.
[Objection:] Surely, that in which these properties reside is itself the conscious entity — why should it not be so? [Reply:] No, because [<s>Buddhi</s>] undergoes transformation, being of the nature of non-eternal properties, and because there is non-difference between property and property-bearer.
Those however — the logicians (<s>Tārkikas</s>) and others — who maintain a difference between the two, failing to see the cognition that grasps non-difference such as 'the pot is blue,' should be disregarded.
[Objection:] How can <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primal matter), which is unconscious, be the creator of the world? For whatever is differentiated by name and form is seen to have a conscious creator, like a pot and such.
The world, which is the subject of dispute, is differentiated by name and form; therefore it is conjectured to have a conscious creator. For the conscious [creator], having sketched name and form in the intellect (<s>Buddhi</s>), produces the external pot with the name 'pot' and with the form having a neck and such.
Therefore, even though the pot as the thing to be produced is already established internally in the form of a mental conception, it has the status of an object (<s>karmakāraka</s>) in the expression 'he makes a pot.'

body.text:
atra vadāmaḥ caitanyasya jagadupādānatve jagato jaḍatvānupapattiḥ yat kāryaṃ taccetanakartṛkamiti vyāptyā śarīrī kartā syāt kiṃ ca tathāpi jñānasya caitanyaviśiṣṭasya kṣityādijanakatve mānābhāvaḥ kulālādijñānecchayoḥ kṛtijanakatvenaivānyathāsiddhatvāt īśvarakṛteśca janyatvāt |
atha yaḥ kṛtimān sa jñānavāniti vyāptyā tatsiddhiḥ evaṃ hi yo jñānavān sa sukhītyādivyāptyā sukhamapīśvare syāt aprayojakatvaṃ cet tulyaṃ tavāpi |
karmaiva jagatkāraṇamityapi ye pratipannāste tāvannatyantaṃ pārihartavyāḥ dharmādharmātmakārthānarthalakṣaṇacodanālakṣaṇasya prakṛtyabhedāt buddhyākārapariṇatāyā eva prakṛteraṣṭau bhāvā ityabhyupagamāt /
body.translated_text:
Here we say: if consciousness were the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of the world, then the non-inertness of the world would not be explicable. By the pervasion 'whatever is an effect has a conscious creator,' the embodied self would be the creator. Moreover, even so, there is no evidence for knowledge — that is, consciousness qualified [by knowledge] — being the generator of earth and such, because the knowledge and desire of the potter and such are otherwise explained (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>) merely as the cause of the [potter's] activity, and because [the world] is created by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).
If [it is argued that] by the pervasion 'whoever possesses activity possesses knowledge,' it is established — then by the same [type of] pervasion 'whoever possesses knowledge is happy,' pleasure too would exist in <s>Īśvara</s>. If [it is said that] this has no probative force, the same applies to your [argument] as well.
As for those who maintain that <s>karma</s> (action) alone is the cause of the world — they need not be entirely refuted, because of the non-difference of <s>karma</s> in the form of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), characterized by benefit and harm, defined by injunction (<s>codanā</s>), from <s>Prakṛti</s>, since it is accepted that the eight states (<s>bhāvas</s>) belong to <s>Prakṛti</s> itself, which has transformed into the form of <s>Buddhi</s>.

body.text:
athedānīṃ pramāṇaṃ vivecayāmaḥ |
tat tāvat trividham pratyakṣānugamānāgamabhedāt |
pratyakṣapramākaraṇaṃ pratyakṣam |
liṅgamanumānam |
athātītānāgatayoḥ kathaṃ liṅgabhāvaḥ jātyā dharmādharmātmanā tatsattvāt |
āptavacanaṃ śabdaḥ yathāsminnarapatinilaye gajarathaturagāḥ santīti |
pānthasakalādhyāyavacana(?)manumāne caritārthatvānnopamānamarhati |
body.translated_text:
Now we shall analyze the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).
These are threefold, differentiated as direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and testimony (<s>āgama</s>).
Direct perception is the instrument of perceptual valid cognition (<s>pratyakṣapramākaraṇa</s>).
The inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) constitutes inference.
[Objection:] How can the inferential mark exist for past and future [entities]? [Reply:] Because they exist by virtue of their class nature (<s>jāti</s>), in the form of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
Testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is the word of a reliable authority (<s>āptavacana</s>) — for example, 'In this royal residence there are elephants, chariots, and horses.'
Since the statement of a traveler or a complete reciter [of the Vedas] fulfills its purpose through inference, analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) does not merit [being a separate means of knowledge].

children.translated_text: and tradition (<s>aitihya</s>) — [these are subsumed under] testimony (<s>āgama</s>), for that is clear from the detailed exposition elsewhere.

body.text:
sa cāyaṃ puruṣaḥ pratiśarīraṃ bhinnaḥ |
tathāhi vimatāni śarīrāṇi svasaṃkhyāsaṃkhyeyātmavanti śarīratvāt sampratipannavat kiṃ caivaṃ yathaikasminneva jīvati devadatte śarīre jāte vā ceṣṭāvati vā mṛte vā bhāvopi jātaceṣṭāvān mṛtaḥ kileti loko vyavaharati tathā śarīrāntarepi tathaiva vyavahārāt tasmāt puruṣabhedobhyupeyaḥ |
body.translated_text:
And this <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self) is different for each body.
For thus: the bodies under dispute possess selves whose number corresponds to their own number, because they are bodies — like an accepted [example]. Furthermore, just as when <s>Devadatta</s> alone is alive, when a body is born, active, or dead, people use expressions like 'born,' 'active,' and 'dead' [about him], so too with respect to other bodies, there is the same usage — therefore, the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> must be accepted.

body.text:
ekamevādvitīyamityādiśruteśca kathañcidupacaritārthatvena tathā ātmano hi vibhuniyatvādabhinnadeśakālā ityekatvenocyate ajo hyeko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahātyenāṃ bhuktabhogāmajo 'nya ityādiśruteśca puruṣabhedamavagacchāmaḥ |
kiṃ punarasya prayojanaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ kiṃ tat akhilānarthamūlabhūtāyā avidyāyāḥ sattvātiśayaviśeṣāvirbhūtavidyayā vināśe sati tatpuruṣasya sahajacaitanyātmanāvasthānaṃ tanmokṣāparaparyāyaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ prakṛtipuruṣavivekajñānaṃ ca taddhetuḥ /
body.translated_text:
As for the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) 'One only, without a second' and such — this is to be taken in an indirect sense (<s>upacaritārtha</s>). Since the self (<s>ātman</s>) is omnipresent and eternal, [all selves] occupy the same space and time — hence it is spoken of as 'one.' From the <s>śruti</s> 'The one unborn, enjoying, lies down; the other unborn abandons her, the one whose enjoyments have been consumed' and such, we understand the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>.
What then is the purpose [of this system]? The highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). What is that? When <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which is the root of all misfortune, is destroyed by the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) that has arisen through the manifestation of a special excellence of <s>sattva</s> (goodness), the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s abiding in its innate conscious nature — that is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is another name for the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). And the discriminative knowledge of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>prakṛtipuruṣavivekajñāna</s>) is its cause.

body.text:
nanu prakṛternityatvāt punarapi tamodrekasambhavādavidyāvirbhāvasambhave muktipracyutiḥ syāditi |
naitat dṛḍhatamacittavṛttinirodhalakṣaṇayogabalāt punarudrekānupapatteḥ |
yadāhuḥ sa tu dīrghakālanairantaryasatkārasevito dṛḍhabhūmirvyutthānasaṃskāreṇa na bādhyata iti |
atha nirlepasyāsya mahāpuruṣasya sambandha eva na kuto 'pavarga iti satyamāha kiṃ tu prakṛtereva bandhamokṣau puṃsyupacaryete tadāhuḥ |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] Since <s>Prakṛti</s> is eternal, the resurgence of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) is possible again, and therefore the re-emergence of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is possible, so there would be a fall from liberation. [Reply:] This is not so, because by the power of <s>yoga</s> characterized by the most firmly established cessation of mental modifications (<s>cittavṛttinirodha</s>), a resurgence is not possible. As they have said: 'That [practice] which is attended to for a long time, without interruption, and with devotion, becomes firmly established and is not overwhelmed by the <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) of emergence.' [Objection:] But if this great <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious Self) is untouched [by anything], there is no connection at all — whence then <s>apavarga</s> (liberation)? [Reply:] True, but bondage and liberation belong to <s>Prakṛti</s> alone and are figuratively attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>. As they have said:

body.text:
rūpaiḥ saptabhirevaṃ badhnātyātmānamātmanā prakṛtiḥ /
  saiva ca puruṣasyārthaṃ vimocayatyekarūpeṇa // iti /
body.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself through seven forms; and she herself liberates for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s> through one form.

body.text:
ayamarthaḥ dharmādharmavairāgyāvairāgyaiśvaryānaiśvaryajñānājñānānyaṣṭau prakṛtirūpāṇi tatra jñānavyatiriktaiḥ dharmādharmādyaiḥ saptabhī rūpaiḥ prakṛtirātmanaivātmānaṃ badhnāti ekarūpeṇa jñānākhyena ca vimocayatīti |
yadāhuḥ |
  dharmeṇa gamanamūrdhvaṃ gamanamadhastādbhavatyadharmeṇa /
  jñānena cāpavargo viparyayādiṣyate bandham // iti /
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>adharma</s> (vice), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>avairāgya</s> (non-dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>anaiśvarya</s> (non-sovereignty), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), and <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) — these are the eight forms of <s>Prakṛti</s>. Among these, by the seven forms other than knowledge — namely <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the rest — <s>Prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself; and by the one form called knowledge she liberates. As they have said: 'By <s>dharma</s> (virtue) there is movement upward; by <s>adharma</s> (vice) there is movement downward; by knowledge there is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>); and from the opposite [of knowledge, i.e. ignorance], bondage is taught.'

The rest [of the doctrine] is complete, unblemished, and established as proven in the <s>Siddhānta</s> (settled conclusion) regarding worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) — and is therefore passed over here.

children.translated_text: To him who has shown the root of all misery, who sees the meaning of all <s>tattvas</s> (realities),
whose mind is filled with compassion — to <s>Kapila</s>, homage, homage!

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sāṃkhyārthatattvapradīpikā</s> (Lamp of the Meaning of the Principles of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>) is completed.
